intelligence.enrichment: The Milky Way is our home galaxy and can appear as a faint band of light from a very dark moonless location; beyond it there are many galaxies, and exoplanets are planets discovered revolving around other stars in our galaxy, while life elsewhere in the Universe is not yet known. Moving outward from the Solar System leads first to our galaxy, then to other galaxies; planets around other stars are exoplanets, but finding such planets does not by itself show that life exists there. The learner correctly applies this rule: The Milky Way is our home galaxy and can appear as a faint band of light from a very dark moonless location; beyond it there are many galaxies, and exoplanets are planets discovered revolving around other stars in our galaxy, while life elsewhere in the Universe is not yet known. Anything beyond the Solar System is just a far star, so galaxies, exoplanets, and evidence of life are the same idea.
